summary: Bedrock to Redrock is an interactive Mars atlas and mission simulator that uses NASA data to help people plan trips across the surface. You can explore the map in 2D or 3D, read about rover discoveries, and compare the shortest route with one that follows gentler slopes. The app estimates how long the trip would take on foot or by rover and shows how the terrain and time spent on science affect whether you can get back with time to spare. We built it for the Martian Map challenge to show how orbital imagery, elevation measurements, and rover records can guide the decisions a surface crew would make.
details:
Planning a trip on Mars means deciding what to visit, how to get there, and how much time to leave for the return. We built Bedrock to Redrock for the Martian Map challenge at the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Irbid, Jordan, to let people work through those decisions using NASA data.

You can explore Mars on a flat map or a 3D globe. The Discover panel has 149 mapped mission records, including landings, rover stops, rock samples, and Ingenuity flights. Search for a record, read what the mission found, and jump to its location. The Layers panel lets you see where features such as minerals, dust, and polar ice have been mapped. In Drone View at lower Mount Sharp, you can fly over the terrain, turn on the geology overlay, and follow Curiosity’s mapped traverse.

One example takes you to Berry Hollow, a patch of rock Perseverance studied at Wildcat Ridge in Jezero Crater. You pick a hypothetical landing site, add Berry Hollow as a science stop, and choose whether to include a return leg. The app uses HiRISE elevation data to compare the shortest route with one that favors gentler slopes. In the baseline Marswalk, the shortest walking round trip is 442 meters. With a 90-minute budget, a 30-minute science stop, and a 20-minute reserve, the model leaves 29 minutes to spare. You can change the walking speed or the time at the stop to see whether the same plan still fits. Regional routes use coarser MOLA elevation and give approximate estimates.

You can replay a route as an astronaut or a rover. The preview shows estimated arrival and return times where available and can suggest a travel mode based on the trip and time budget. Route details also show estimated local solar time and daylight. On compatible phones and tablets, Earth GPS Demo uses your movement on Earth to move the simulated explorer on Mars. It offers four distance scales, from 1× to 1000×, with written and spoken guidance. Supported devices can also control the camera and compass by tilting. Detailed turns and detours depend on local terrain coverage. The global map and the Wildcat Ridge and Gale Crater terrain packs are available as offline downloads.
